findings.title: The Profit Gap is running through your discount line
findings.evidence: 23 of your 69 live products are discounted, averaging 17.0% off. That can hold your revenue while contribution profit slips underneath it. The gap between the two is the first number RISE looks at.
findings.week_one: Before a dollar of spend moves, we model where money is made or lost, discounts included.

findings.title: No subscribe-and-save path for repeat buyers
findings.evidence: Your storefront runs 69 products with no subscription option we could find on the page. Repeat purchases are where contribution profit compounds, and a subscribe-and-save path turns one-time buyers into predictable revenue on the traffic you already pay for.
findings.week_one: A subscription option is a store decision on your side. It compounds every profitable order the paid engine buys.

findings.title: Your price band is wide and the median sits low
findings.evidence: Catalog runs $5.49 to $299.99 with a $26.99 median. A wide band with a low median makes blended AOV fragile on paid. The lever is threshold and bundle offers on the landing path the ads point to.
findings.week_one: We point spend at the offers and price points that hold blended profit. Bundle and threshold builds on the store are yours to green-light.

findings.title: Paid clicks are landing on sold-out variants
findings.evidence: 42.5% of your variants read out-of-stock right now. Every paid click that hits a sold-out variant is spend with no shot at converting, a direct drag on blended MER.
findings.week_one: We prune sold-out items out of your product feeds and spend routing in the first optimization pass. Restocking is your call.

findings.title: You're not running paid social right now
findings.evidence: The public Meta Ad Library shows zero ads for this brand. For a brand at your catalog depth, that's unclaimed demand, and a cold-audience paid engine is the fastest lever we pull.
findings.week_one: Multi-network ads management targeted at your ideal customer, optimized for profit from the first campaign.

findings.title: No visible reviews on the page paid traffic hits
findings.evidence: We couldn't find review markup on your product page. Cold paid traffic converts on social proof, so surfacing reviews on the PDP is a direct conversion lever.
findings.week_one: Getting reviews visible on the product page is a store change on your side. Cold traffic buys on proof.
